title: Failure Attribution and Evaluation Reliability Framework for LongMemEval

citation.apa: Guo, B. (2026). Failure attribution and evaluation reliability framework for LongMemEval (Version 2.0 RC3) [Methodology report]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23273896
citation.chicago: Guo, Baixin. "Failure Attribution and Evaluation Reliability Framework for LongMemEval." Methodology report, Version 2.0 RC3. Zenodo, 2026. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23273896.
citation.mla: Guo, Baixin. Failure Attribution and Evaluation Reliability Framework for LongMemEval. Version 2.0 RC3, Zenodo, 2026, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23273896.

abstract: The methods half of the Boundary Labs collaboration, deposited on its own and registered on Zenodo as the supplement to the joint preprint "What the Score Measured" (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22980060), which reports the reconstruction, the repaired harness and the rerun. This report carries the instrument rather than the run. It reads one failed answer along four separate scales: outcome correctness (O-C, O-I, O-D, O-U), what evidence is actually available (E0 to E4), how far a failure can be attributed to a stage (A0 to A3), and how much confidence the judgment itself carries (J0 to J3). It adds a T1-T5 diagnostic test matrix naming the claim each test can support, and a blind four-rater judging protocol applied to 150 prediction-judgment instances - 25 cases scored under six conditions, not 150 distinct questions. Retrieval and reader-context validation are marked collaborator-reported and were not independently recomputed; the fixed-transcript reader replay (T4) is left unexecuted, so no new E4, A2 or A3 conclusions come from it. Original benchmark scores and hand judgments are preserved unchanged. A public versioned report, not a peer-reviewed publication; no conference submission or acceptance is claimed.
